findings.title: Clone action icon deviates from carried-forward spec
findings.problem: Story spec (2026-10-07 revision, explicitly carried forward/not superseded) calls for a new src/assets/icons/clone.svg to be used on the Clone row action to distinguish it from Copy ID's copy.svg. The shipped diff instead leaves Clone on the original CopySvg (copy.svg) and introduces a new ClipboardSvg (clipboard.svg) assigned to Copy ID instead. No clone.svg asset exists anywhere in the repo.
findings.impact: Icons are visually distinct by accident (CopySvg vs ClipboardSvg) rather than by the documented design intent; a future reader or agent trusting the story doc will look for a clone.svg asset that was never created, and the spec-vs-shipped-UI mismatch goes unresolved.
findings.recommendation: Either add clone.svg and assign it to the Clone action per the carried-forward spec, or get explicit sign-off to amend the story/spec to match the shipped ClipboardSvg-on-Copy-ID design, then update the carried-forward revision note accordingly.

findings.title: Clone form carries source secrets without stripping or disclosure
findings.problem: getFormValuesFromServer() (reused unchanged from Edit) pre-fills the Clone modal's serverConfig textarea with JSON.stringify(cloneSource.config, ...) verbatim, including any auth_token/header credential/secret env values, then submits that data through cloneConfigFromForm to POST v1/mcp-configs/{id}/clone with no client-side redaction and no user-facing notice, where the previous flow explicitly stripped and flagged these fields.
findings.impact: Any secret present on the source MCP server config is silently duplicated into the newly cloned configuration and round-tripped through the UI and network request body, with no disclosure to the admin performing the clone.
findings.recommendation: Confirm this matches the current backend contract and is the already-agreed scope decision documented in story.md's Non-Goals (masking/stripping explicitly removed); if so, record that explicitly in the MR description. If the backend still strips secrets, or the verbatim-copy behavior was not meant to ship unflagged, reintroduce redaction/a user notice before submit.
